evidence_checks.located_span: Years ago before I carried a laptop everyday I used a leather bag for work and court. just too heavy with lap top.
evidence_checks.note: Work bag too heavy with a laptop. Does not say it was carried on the shoulder or that it caused pain, only that it was too heavy.

evidence_checks.located_span: I liked the idea of a leather tote and I have one but I find the bag itself before filled is already so heavy and then to add all my stuff makes it worse.
evidence_checks.note: Work tote is too heavy. The comment does not mention a laptop; the laptop link comes only from the parent post's request.

evidence_checks.located_span: I switched to an Aer backpack to save my back since I carry a laptop, but if I didn’t have to I’d go tote all the way.
evidence_checks.note: Suggests that a tote with a laptop strains the back. This is implied by the switch rather than stated as felt pain.

evidence_checks.located_span: it hurts my shoulders to carry a laptop, notebook, and water bottle in there for a day
evidence_checks.note: Direct statement: a tote with a laptop hurts the shoulders.

evidence_checks.located_span: I really messed up my right shoulder by using a shoulder bag to carry my laptop and other work stuffs daily
evidence_checks.note: Direct statement: a shoulder bag with a laptop for work caused a shoulder injury.

evidence_checks.located_span: walking around in the heat with a tote bag is killing my shoulder and back
evidence_checks.note: Work-commute tote pain, but the listed contents (book, water, meals, medications) do not include a laptop, so it does not match the laptop wording of the claim.

evidence_checks.located_span: I love the look of a tote, but carrying my laptop around all day is absolutely destroying my shoulders.
evidence_checks.note: Direct statement: a laptop in a tote hurts the shoulders. The use is work and study, not only work.

evidence_checks.located_span: my shoulder hurts almost immediately because of my tote bag
evidence_checks.note: Work tote that carries a laptop, notebook, lunch and chargers causes shoulder pain.

evidence_checks.located_span: I get shoulder pain from lugging around my larger totes and I’m heartbroken!
evidence_checks.note: Shoulder pain from large totes, with work implied by 'work backpack'. A laptop is not mentioned.

scope_issue: Some cited items (E-0276, E-0377, and the E-0147 comment itself) do not mention a laptop. E-0121 does not specify a shoulder carry or pain. The claim is otherwise within its stated scope.
reasoning: At least six distinct threads (E-0121, E-0157, E-0191, E-0227, E-0288, E-0348) have people who carry a laptop for work saying a tote or shoulder bag is too heavy or hurts the shoulder or back, so the pattern wording 'several independent discussions' holds. The contradicting items do not refute the claim. E-0331 is one person for whom a tote works after a backpack injury, E-0372 actually says one shoulder is too heavy, and E-0378 blames the contents rather than denying the strain.

evidence_checks.located_span: I switched to an Aer backpack to save my back since I carry a laptop
evidence_checks.note: Stated reason for switching: protecting the back because she carries a laptop.

evidence_checks.located_span: I really messed up my right shoulder by using a shoulder bag to carry my laptop and other work stuffs daily… now I use a backpack
evidence_checks.note: Shoulder injury from a laptop in a shoulder bag, followed by a move to a backpack. The cause is implied by the sequence.

evidence_checks.located_span: I switched in my 20s after having severe shoulder pain that carrying a handbag was exacerbating.
evidence_checks.note: Pain is the reason for switching, but the bag was a handbag and there is no laptop. This supports the general pain-driven switch, not the laptop-specific one.

evidence_checks.located_span: Day 1 of taking public transit to work with a tote bag and I immediately bought a backpack.
evidence_checks.note: No pain, heaviness or laptop is stated. The reason for switching is left unsaid.

evidence_checks.located_span: walking around in the heat with a tote bag is killing my shoulder and back
evidence_checks.note: Pain led to buying a backpack, but the contents listed exclude a laptop.

evidence_checks.located_span: I switched to a backpack to save my back/shoulder.
evidence_checks.note: Pain-driven switch away from a tote. The comment does not name a laptop; it is in a thread about laptop work-bag pain.

evidence_checks.located_span: I carry similar items and have a similar walk. I moved into a Tumi backpack and my shoulders and back have never been happier.
evidence_checks.note: 'Similar items' refers to the parent's laptop load. The switch is linked to shoulder and back comfort.

evidence_checks.located_span: giving up my Seau Sangle and never felt better.
evidence_checks.note: A pain-driven switch from a large tote, but there is no laptop.

scope_issue: Several cited items (E-0229, E-0230, E-0275, E-0384) are not about a laptop, and E-0230 states no pain at all. The laptop-specific support rests on E-0157, E-0227, E-0368 and E-0376.
reasoning: The claim is modest ('some people'), and E-0157, E-0227 and E-0376 explicitly or near-explicitly give shoulder or back strain from a laptop load as the reason for switching to a backpack. E-0331 and E-0372 show that backpacks hurt some other people. This limits how far the claim generalizes but does not contradict it.

evidence_checks.located_span: if I didn’t have to I’d go tote all the way
evidence_checks.note: A comfort switcher who says she would still prefer a tote. She does not call the backpack less attractive.

evidence_checks.located_span: I don’t like my current backpack as it’s pretty bulky and not very professional looking.
evidence_checks.note: Calls a backpack unprofessional, but the poster is not described as someone who moved from a tote to a backpack for comfort.

evidence_checks.located_span: I understand that a backpack is less aesthetic, but not everything has to be aesthetic
evidence_checks.note: A comfort switcher concedes the backpack looks worse, but is content and does not want a tote back.

evidence_checks.located_span: I’ll admit it’s a bit silly with my blouse and pants. and makes me look like a middle schooler again.
evidence_checks.note: A comfort switcher describes the backpack as looking silly or juvenile with work clothes.

evidence_checks.located_span: I just succumbed to a really ugly backpack that carries weight well.
evidence_checks.note: A reluctant switch for weight carrying; the backpack is called ugly.

evidence_checks.located_span: I’ve had to make peace with using a low profile, polished looking backpack
evidence_checks.note: Shows reluctance (implies a preference against it), but she calls the backpack polished, not less attractive.

evidence_checks.located_span: I didn’t get a stylish backpack but it doesn’t matter cos I am no longer in pain!
evidence_checks.note: Implies the backpack is not stylish, but says this does not matter. There is no wish to return to a tote.

scope_issue: 'Often' implies a frequency the sources cannot show. Only E-0157 explicitly says she would prefer a tote, and E-0351 only implies it. Several switchers (E-0255, E-0384) accept the backpack without wanting a tote back, and E-0181 is not a comfort switcher.
reasoning: Several comfort switchers do describe their backpack as less aesthetic, silly or ugly (E-0255, E-0277, E-0290, E-0384), so the first half has reasonable support. The 'would still prefer a tote' half rests mainly on E-0157. E-0225 (a long-time switcher who is happy with a well-made, good-looking backpack), along with E-0255 and E-0384 who say looks don't matter, cut against 'often'. That tension is not resolved.

evidence_checks.located_span: I have a smallish MZ Wallace that I use when I don’t need to carry a lot
evidence_checks.note: A lighter bag on light days. The same post also says she uses a separate small handbag alongside.

evidence_checks.located_span: Most days, it’s a fjallraven kanken backpack. If I don’t need to carry as much, a small purse and/or lunch bag.
evidence_checks.note: Explicit split by load: backpack versus a small purse.

evidence_checks.located_span: If I’m just going to a coffee shop or something I may just put my laptop in a tote bag since I have less to carry.
evidence_checks.note: Split by load. The light-load case is a coffee-shop trip, not a work day.

evidence_checks.located_span: Big enough to hold most of my personal stuff, and I carry it to work along with a laptop bag
evidence_checks.note: Two bags carried together. Load is not stated as the motive.

evidence_checks.located_span: So for meeting would bring the mulberry and longchamp for daily use
evidence_checks.note: The split is by occasion or formality (meeting versus daily), not by load, although lightness is the reason for daily use.
Describes using a backpack instead of a tote. There is no split between bags.

evidence_checks.located_span: When I'm carrying a heavier load I carry a monos metro
evidence_checks.note: Explicit switch of bag by load.

evidence_checks.located_span: I separately carry my Uniqlo dumpling bag for things I need easy access to (phone, keys, sunglasses, lipbalm etc)
evidence_checks.note: Two bags carried together. The motive is easy access, not load.

evidence_checks.located_span: the fact that the weight is distributed between two bags and not one bag digging into your shoulder at the same spot makes a huge difference for me
evidence_checks.note: Two bags carried together explicitly to spread the weight.
Leaving the laptop at the office reduces the load. It is not a split between bags.

evidence_checks.located_span: recently I started to notice a lot of people carry more than one bag for work if that’s an option or would help (e.g. laptop + essentials in one / gym clothes + makeup bag in another)
evidence_checks.note: A secondhand observation that people carry more than one bag for work.

scope_issue: The sources do not support 'many people'; the stated scope itself says this is not a measure of how common it is. Several two-bag cases (E-0189, E-0322, E-0174) are motivated by access or convenience rather than load, so 'split by load' over-attributes the motive. E-0209, E-0248 and E-0370 do not show the behaviour.
reasoning: The behaviour is documented across several threads: different bags by load (E-0124, E-0152, E-0161, E-0301) and two bags at once to spread weight (E-0358). However, 'many' is an unsupported quantifier, and some two-bag examples have a convenience motive rather than a load motive. E-0174 (two bags out of laziness about transferring items) qualifies the motive rather than contradicting the behaviour.

evidence_checks.located_span: But do take note the bag's got a weight to it when it's empty, so it will get quite heavy when you do put stuff in it.
evidence_checks.note: Notes the empty weight as a caution, but the main reasons for not recommending are price and shipping. The material is not called leather or structured. Weak at best.

evidence_checks.located_span: However, it's entirely too heavy. (3.6 lbs empty)
evidence_checks.note: Rejects the Cuyana Forma explicitly because of its empty weight. The text does not say whether it is leather or structured.

evidence_checks.located_span: I find the bag itself before filled is already so heavy
evidence_checks.note: A leather tote is heavy before it is filled; she moved to lighter totes.

evidence_checks.located_span: I wanted to love this backpack (got it in hazelnut), but unfortunately underestimated how heavy leather can be.
evidence_checks.note: Regrets a leather bag's weight. Empty weight is implied rather than stated.

evidence_checks.located_span: is your bag heavy on its own when it’s empty? If that’s the case, you gotta get a new bag.
evidence_checks.note: Explicitly advises checking empty weight. The same comment regrets the Cuyana tote being heavy.

evidence_checks.located_span: Tumi backpacks are so structured that: (1) it’s too heavy even when empty
evidence_checks.note: Regrets a structured bag that is too heavy when empty.

evidence_checks.located_span: The Beis is already 2.75 pounds before you put anything in it.
evidence_checks.note: Checks empty weight when evaluating a bag.

scope_issue: Examples include backpacks (Tumi, the leather backpack), not only totes. E-0081 is about a Nordace backpack whose material is not stated as leather or structured and which was not rejected mainly for weight.
reasoning: Multiple independent comments check or cite a bag's empty weight and reject or regret leather or structured bags for it (E-0105, E-0147, E-0293, E-0357, E-0373, E-0394), which supports the hedged 'some shoppers' wording. The contradicting items (E-0378, E-0399) say the contents also matter. That is an alternative factor, not a refutation, and the stated scope already acknowledges it.
